title: Coarse graining with sampled g(r) origins and iinit 1
purpose: Exercises the coarse-graining option of the `epsr` engine of EPSR [@soper1996,@soper2005], on when the first value of `qinscalefc` is > 1: per-molecule size factors `scalefacmol` (`.ato` molecule headers) and per-type sphere parameters `natomsph radminsph radmaxsph cgmolfac` define form factors and scale the reference-potential distances of molecule pairs [@epsrmanual]. This case combines coarse graining with random sampling of g(r) origin molecules and a one-value `qinscalefc`.
system: The EPSR-test system: a liquid mixture of 200 dimethyl sulphoxide (DMSO, (CH3)2SO) and 400 water molecules (DMSO mole fraction 1/3; 3200 atoms) at 300 K in a cubic box of side 33.12 Å (atomic number density 0.0881 atoms/Å³). DMSO uses EPSR's Lennard-Jones + Coulomb reference potential with methyl rotational groups; water uses SPC/E Lennard-Jones and charge parameters [@berendsen1987] with EPSR's flexible intramolecular geometry (O-H 0.976 Å). The empirical potential is refined against three neutron diffraction data sets of deuterated DMSO in D2O, in null-scattering H2O/D2O and in H2O (ISIS SANDALS runs SLS03863, SLS03871, SLS03850), the isotope-substitution approach of Soper and Luzar [@soperluzar1992]. Coarse graining represents atoms by uniform spheres (form factors from `gaussianqr2` of the inner and outer radius); a molecule pair scales the reference-potential distance by `scalefac = 0.5*(scalefacmol(i)+scalefacmol(j))`. Here DMSO `scalefacmol` is 1.0 and water 0.9/1.0/1.1/1.3; O1 `3.0 0.0 1.6 1.0` and H1 `2.0 0.1 0.5 1.0` have `natomsph` > 1, which gives a non-zero self-term correction `selfcorr` in `intraformfactor`.
inputs: Generated from EPSR-test by `scripts/make_cg.py <folder> <mode>` (edits `.EPSR.inp` keywords, the `.ato` `scalefacmol` words and type columns). Mode for this case: `.EPSR.inp` `qinscalefc 1.2` (one value, so `selfbroadpwr` defaults to 0), `ntimes 2`, `ngrsamples 150`, `iinit 1` (accumulators reset); `.ato` as above.
verification: With `ngrsamples 150` the `atogen` acceptance probability is 0.25 (150 of 600 molecules), so origin molecules are chosen with the random-number generator, `addwav` = 1 and `wavinter` is filled for all partner molecules; the random-number state in the `.ato` stays identical. The three form-factor files are compared byte for byte with the standard outputs.
notes: Single-precision quirk reproduced: int(0.4/0.2) is 1, so O1/H1 get 2 bins. Fortran: form factors and `wavinter` are computed but never used for S(Q) (the coarse-graining code in `gensq` is commented out).
